summary: A correctly-built, signal-only, fail-safe doorbell. All four ACs hold; gate GREEN (selftest 2544); 3 teeth reproduced independently non-vacuous; 8 capabilities.yaml byte-identical; repo-only placement confirmed. Signal-only is STRUCTURAL: no inbound/reply-reading path exists (grep-confirmed), TelegramSink discards the send response, the notice points at the tracker and carries no approve/decide action - nothing advances a request through this module. Fail-safe confirmed (send wrapped in try/except, never raises; urllib imported inside TelegramSink.send so never on the gate path). The notes are PRE-LIVE-WIRING gates, not defects in the shipped review-stage module, which cannot send to a live channel today (main runs only selfcheck; TelegramSink is never constructed; no ring_from_repo).

criteria.note: build_notice returns (notice_text, jira_link) from read-only record fields; no inbound path (grep for getUpdates/webhook/poll/answerCallback/thread/subprocess = none); notice says 'Decide in the tracker'; records byte-unchanged after a run.

SEND is an injected sink; gate drives FakeSink/FailingSink (no network); real TelegramSink resolves a secret-reference token, fails closed, urllib imported inside send so never gate-run. try/except Exception returns outcome:failed, never raises.

Idempotent per (request_id,status) via notice_key; status change re-notifies; proven in-gate. NOTE (must-fix-before-live): the marker is FakeSink's in-memory set; TelegramSink keeps NO durable marker and always sends, so a fresh sink per live run would re-notify (spam) - a durable keyed store (or reconciler-only drive) is required before live use. Redaction runs on the whole body via the reused W3 redactor.
Non-tautological selftest over FakeSink; 3 teeth reproduced independently from a standalone script, each RED with the module sha256 byte-unchanged.

findings.text: Finding 1 (must-fix-before-live, RULE #3): declared operating-term redaction is exercised only in the test fixture - the module has NO wiring to pull projection.sensitive_terms, and every in-module call passes terms=(). Confirmed: build_notice with no terms emits 'MRR 45000, LTV 312, CAC 40' in the clear. The live caller MUST pass projection.get('sensitive_terms') exactly as W3's _project_one does, or a live send leaks operating data to Telegram.

Finding 2 (must-fix-before-live): durable idempotency marker. TelegramSink always attempts a send and the module ships no durable store; a naive fresh-sink-per-run live deployment spams. A durable keyed store, or driving only via the reconciler, must exist before live use.

Finding 3 (inherited W3 declared-scope limit): the redactor is not a secret backstop - a raw credential literal or a URL query-token in bound_artifact.ref / tracker.url bypasses it (confirmed: sk-live-.../JWT and ?auth=SECRET123 pass through). Given the destination is a real external channel, consider an undeclared-secret heuristic before the live edge.

Finding 4 (minor): ring's try covers only sink.send; build_notice/notice_key run before it, so a malformed record passed directly to ring (bypassing ring_all's dict-guard + W2 validation) could raise. Low severity (records are W2-validated upstream). Broaden the try or document ring requires a W2-validated dict.
